title.zh: 卷三十六 志第六: 兵衞志下
title.raw: 卷三十六 志第六: 兵衞志下 Volume 36 Treatises 6: Military 3

translations.literal: Military Guards, Part 3 ○ Five Capitals Militia Levies
translations.idiomatic: Military Guards, Part 3 — Five Capitals Militia Levies

sentences.zh: 遼建五京：臨潢，契丹故壤；

translations.literal: Liao established five capitals: Linhuang, the old Khitan homeland;
translations.idiomatic: The Liao founded five capitals—Linhuang in the old Khitan heartland;

sentences.zh: 遼陽，漢之遼東，為渤海故國；

translations.literal: Liaoyang, Han-era Liaodong, the former Bohai realm;
translations.idiomatic: Liaoyang, the Han Liaodong region and former Bohai state;

sentences.zh: 中京，漢遼西地，自唐以來契丹有之。

translations.literal: Zhongjing, Han Liaoxi territory, held by the Khitan since Tang times.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing in Han Liaoxi, which the Khitan had held since Tang.

sentences.zh: 三京丁籍可紀者二十二萬六千一百，蕃漢轉戶為多。

translations.literal: The three capitals' registrable ding totaled two hundred twenty-six thousand one hundred; Fan and Han rotating households were the majority.
translations.idiomatic: Among the three capitals, registrable levies came to 226,100—mostly Fan and Han rotating households.

sentences.zh: 析津、大同、故漢地，籍丁八十萬六千七百。

translations.literal: Xijin, Datong, and other former Han lands registered eight hundred six thousand seven hundred ding.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han districts such as Xijin and Datong listed 806,700 militia levies.

sentences.zh: 契丹本戶多隸宮帳、部族，其餘蕃漢戶丁分隸者，皆不與焉。

translations.literal: Most native Khitan households were attached to palace tents and tribes; other Fan and Han household ding assigned elsewhere were not included.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan core families mostly fell under palace tents and tribes, so other Fan and Han levies assigned elsewhere were excluded from these rolls.

translations.literal: Taizu built the imperial capital at Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu founded the imperial capital at Linhuang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗定晉，晉主石敬瑭來獻十六城，乃定四京，改皇都為上京。

translations.literal: Taizong settled Jin; Jin ruler Shi Jingtang presented sixteen prefectures, then four capitals were fixed and the imperial capital was renamed Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong pacified Jin, Shi Jingtang of Later Jin ceded sixteen prefectures; the court then fixed four capitals and renamed the imperial seat Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 有丁一十六萬七千二百。

translations.literal: It had one hundred sixty-seven thousand two hundred ding.

translations.idiomatic: Linhuang Prefecture — Linhuang County registered 7,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Zu Prefecture Prefecture: Changba County, 4,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Zu Prefecture Prefecture, Changba County counted 4,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Huai Prefecture Prefecture: Fuyu County, 3,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Huai Prefecture Prefecture, Fuyu County counted 3,000 militia levies.

sentences.zh: 慶州玄寧縣丁一萬二千。

translations.literal: Qing Prefecture Prefecture, Xuanning County, 12,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Prefecture Prefecture — Xuanning County: 12,000 militia levies.

sentences.zh: 泰州興國縣丁一千四百。

translations.literal: Tai Prefecture Prefecture, Xingguo County, 1,400 ding.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Prefecture Prefecture — Xingguo County: 1,400 militia levies.

translations.literal: Changchun Prefecture Prefecture, Changchun County, 4,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: Changchun Prefecture Prefecture — Changchun County: 4,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Wu Prefecture Prefecture, Aimin County, 2,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Prefecture Prefecture — Aimin County: 2,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Yong Prefecture Prefecture: Changning County, 9,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Yong Prefecture Prefecture, Changning County counted 9,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Yikun Prefecture Prefecture, Guangyi County, 5,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: Yikun Prefecture Prefecture — Guangyi County: 5,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Longhua Prefecture Prefecture, Longhua County, 2,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: Longhua Prefecture Prefecture — Longhua County: 2,000 militia levies.

sentences.zh: 降聖州永安縣丁一千五百。

translations.literal: Jiangsheng Prefecture Prefecture, Yongan County, 1,500 ding.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsheng Prefecture Prefecture — Yongan County: 1,500 militia levies.

translations.literal: Rao Prefecture Prefecture: Changle County, 8,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Rao Prefecture Prefecture, Changle County counted 8,000 militia levies.
Under the court's direct retainers, Hui Prefecture listed 20,000 militia levies.

sentences.zh: 東京，本渤海，以其地建南京遼陽府。

translations.literal: Eastern Capital: originally Bohai; its territory became Nanjing Liaoyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital began as Bohai; the Liao built Nanjing Liaoyang Prefecture on that ground.

sentences.zh: 統縣六，轄軍、府、州、城二十六，有丁四萬一千四百。

translations.literal: It governed six counties, twenty-six armies, prefectures, and walled posts, with forty-one thousand four hundred ding.
translations.idiomatic: It ruled six counties and twenty-six military prefectures and cities, with 41,400 levies on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 天顯十三年，太宗改為東京。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianxian, Taizong renamed it Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxian year 13 Taizong redesignated it the Eastern Capital.
Liaoyang Prefecture — Liaoyang County registered 3,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Kai Prefecture Prefecture: Kaiyuan County, 2,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Kai Prefecture Prefecture, Kaiyuan County counted 2,000 militia levies.

sentences.zh: 定州：定東縣丁一千六百。

translations.literal: Ding Prefecture Prefecture: Dingdong County, 1,600 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Ding Prefecture Prefecture, Dingdong County counted 1,600 militia levies.

translations.literal: Bao Prefecture Prefecture: Laiyuan County, 2,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Bao Prefecture Prefecture, Laiyuan County counted 2,000 militia levies.

sentences.zh: 南京析津府，統縣十一，轄軍、府、州、城九，有丁五十六萬六千。

translations.literal: Southern Capital Xijin Prefecture governed eleven counties, nine armies, prefectures, and cities, with five hundred sixty-six thousand ding.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's Xijin Prefecture held eleven counties and nine subordinate commands, listing 566,000 militia levies.
Xijin Prefecture — Xijin County registered 40,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Shun Prefecture Prefecture, Huairou County, 10,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: Shun Prefecture Prefecture — Huairou County: 10,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Tan Prefecture Prefecture: Miyun County, 10,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Tan Prefecture Prefecture, Miyun County counted 10,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Zhuo Prefecture Prefecture: Fanyang County, 20,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuo Prefecture Prefecture, Fanyang County counted 20,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Yi Prefecture Prefecture: Yi County, 50,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Yi Prefecture Prefecture, Yi County counted 50,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Ji Prefecture Prefecture: Yuyang County, 8,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Ji Prefecture Prefecture, Yuyang County counted 8,000 militia levies.

sentences.zh: 平州：盧龍縣丁一萬四千。

translations.literal: Ping Prefecture Prefecture: Lulong County, 14,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Ping Prefecture Prefecture, Lulong County counted 14,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Luan Prefecture Prefecture: Yifeng County, 8,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Luan Prefecture Prefecture, Yifeng County counted 8,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Ying Prefecture Prefecture: Guangning County, 6,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Ying Prefecture Prefecture, Guangning County counted 6,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Jing Prefecture Prefecture: Zunhua County, 6,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Jing Prefecture Prefecture, Zunhua County counted 6,000 militia levies.

sentences.zh: 西京大同府，統縣七，轄軍、府、州、城十七，有丁三十二萬二千七百。

translations.literal: Western Capital Datong Prefecture governed seven counties, seventeen armies, prefectures, and cities, with three hundred twenty-two thousand seven hundred ding.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing Datong Prefecture ruled seven counties and seventeen military jurisdictions, with 322,700 levies recorded.
Datong Prefecture — Datong County registered 20,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Hong Prefecture Prefecture: Yongning County, 20,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Prefecture Prefecture, Yongning County counted 20,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: De Prefecture Prefecture: Xuande County, 6,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At De Prefecture Prefecture, Xuande County counted 6,000 militia levies.

sentences.zh: 豐州：富民縣丁二千四百。

translations.literal: Feng Prefecture Prefecture: Fumin County, 2,400 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Feng Prefecture Prefecture, Fumin County counted 2,400 militia levies.
Zhenwu County raised 300 militia levies of local militia.

sentences.zh: 奉聖州：永興縣丁一萬六千。

translations.literal: Fengsheng Prefecture Prefecture: Yongxing County, 16,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengsheng Prefecture Prefecture, Yongxing County counted 16,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Guihua Prefecture Prefecture: Wende County, 20,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Guihua Prefecture Prefecture, Wende County counted 20,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Kehan Prefecture Prefecture: Huailai County, 6,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Kehan Prefecture Prefecture, Huailai County counted 6,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Ru Prefecture Prefecture: Jinshan County, 10,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Ru Prefecture Prefecture, Jinshan County counted 10,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Yu Prefecture Prefecture: Lingxian County, 40,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Yu Prefecture Prefecture, Lingxian County counted 40,000 militia levies.

sentences.zh: 應州：金城縣丁一萬六千。

translations.literal: Ying Prefecture Prefecture: Jincheng County, 16,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Ying Prefecture Prefecture, Jincheng County counted 16,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Shuo Prefecture Prefecture: Shanyang County, 8,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Shuo Prefecture Prefecture, Shanyang County counted 8,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Jinsu Army autumn-defense troops, one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinsu Army posted 1,000 troops for autumn defense.

translations.literal: Wu Prefecture Prefecture: Shenwu County, 10,000 ding.
translations.idiomatic: At Wu Prefecture Prefecture, Shenwu County counted 10,000 militia levies.

translations.literal: Heqing Army autumn-defense troops, one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Heqing Army likewise fielded 1,000 autumn-defense troops.

sentences.zh: 聖宗統和二十三年，城七金山，建大定府，號中京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Tonghe, Shengzong walled Qijin Mountain and founded Zhongjing at Dading Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzong's Tonghe year 23 saw Qijin Mountain fortified and Zhongjing established at Dading Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 統縣九，轄軍、府、州、城二十三。

translations.literal: It governed nine counties and twenty-three armies, prefectures, and cities.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing governed nine counties and twenty-three military prefectures and posts.

sentences.zh: 草創末定，丁籍莫考，可見者一縣：高州三韓縣丁一萬。

translations.literal: Still in early founding and not yet fixed; ding rolls were unverified—only one county is visible: Gaozhou Sanhan County, ten thousand ding.
translations.idiomatic: Because the seat was newly founded, levies were not fully tallied; only Gaozhou's Sanhan County is recorded at 10,000 ding.

sentences.zh: 大約五京民丁可見者，一百一十萬七千三百為鄉兵。

translations.literal: Roughly, visible militia ding of the Five Capitals totaled one million one hundred seven thousand three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the Five Capitals' visible militia rolls came to about 1,107,300 levies.

sentences.zh: 遼屬國可紀者五十有九，朝貢無常。

translations.literal: Liao subject states that can be recorded number fifty-nine; tribute audiences were irregular.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-nine subject states appear in the records, though tribute missions had no fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 有事則遣使征兵，或下詔專征；

translations.literal: When affairs arose the court sent envoys to levy troops, or issued edicts for dedicated campaigns;
translations.idiomatic: In emergencies the court dispatched envoys to raise troops or issued edicts ordering separate expeditions;

translations.literal: Those who did not comply were attacked.
translations.idiomatic: States that refused were punished by force.

sentences.zh: 助軍眾寡，各從其便，無常額。

translations.literal: Auxiliary forces varied in size at each state's convenience; there was no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Contributed forces followed each realm's means, with no standing quota.

sentences.zh: 又有鐵不得國者，興宗重熙十七年乞以兵助攻夏國，詔不許。

translations.literal: There was also the Iron-Forbidden State: in Shengzong's Chongxi year 17 it begged troops to assist the attack on Western Xia; the edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Iron-Forbidden State once asked in Chongxi year 17 to join an attack on Western Xia; the court denied the request.

sentences.zh: 遼之為國，鄰於梁、唐、晉、漢、周、宋。

translations.literal: As a state Liao neighbored Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, Zhou, and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Liao bordered in turn Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, Zhou, and Song.

sentences.zh: 晉以恩故，始則父子一家，終則寇讎相攻；

translations.literal: Jin began as father and son in one household because of favor, yet ended with raiding and mutual attack;
translations.idiomatic: With Later Jin the bond began as kin-by-grace yet closed in mutual raids;

translations.literal: Liang, Tang, and Zhou were plainly one enemy state each.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, Tang, and Zhou each stood as a full rival power.

sentences.zh: 宋惟太宗征北漢，遼不能救，餘多敗衄，縱得亦不償失。

translations.literal: Song only in Taizong's northern Han campaign did Liao fail to save them; most other clashes ended in defeat, and even victories did not repay the cost.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Song's Taizong attacked Northern Han could Liao not relieve the target; otherwise Liao mostly lost, and wins rarely paid for themselves.

sentences.zh: 良由石晉獻土，中國失五關之固然也。

translations.literal: This truly stemmed from Shi Jingtang's cession of territory and China's loss of the five passes' natural strength.
translations.idiomatic: The root cause was Shi Jingtang's land grant and the Central States' forfeiture of the five passes' natural defenses.

sentences.zh: 高麗小邦，屢喪遼兵，非以險阻足恃故歟。

translations.literal: Goryeo was a small state yet repeatedly cost Liao armies—was it not because its terrain was hard to rely on?
translations.idiomatic: Small Goryeo still drained Liao forces again and again—perhaps its rugged ground alone could explain it.

sentences.zh: 西夏彈丸之地，南敗宋，東抗遼。

translations.literal: Western Xia was a tiny realm yet defeated Song in the south and resisted Liao in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Western Xia, though minute, beat Song to the south and held Liao at bay in the east.

sentences.zh: 雖西北士馬雄勁，元昊、諒祚智勇過人，能使党項、阻卜掣肘大國，蓋亦襟山帶河，有以助其勢耳。

translations.literal: Though northwestern horses and warriors were strong, Yuanhao and Liangzuo were surpassingly clever and brave, enabling Tangut and Zubu forces to check a great power—surely mountains and rivers at their backs helped their momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Even with strong northwestern cavalry, Yuanhao and Liangzuo's talent let Tangut and Zubu allies tie down a great empire, aided by mountains and rivers at their flank.

sentences.zh: 雖然，宋久失地利，而舊《志》言兵，唯以敵宋為務。

translations.literal: Even so, Song long lacked terrain advantage, yet the old Monograph on troops treated Song alone as the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Song had lost terrain for years while older records still framed warfare chiefly against Song.

sentences.zh: 逾三關，聚議北京，猶不敢輕進。

translations.literal: Crossing three passes and massing councils at Beijing, they still dared not advance lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Even after crossing the three passes and gathering councils at Beijing, Liao hesitated to push forward.

sentences.zh: 豈不以大河在前，三鎮在後，臨事好謀之審，不容不然歟。

translations.literal: Was it not because the Yellow River lay ahead and the three garrisons behind, and careful counsel at the moment could not permit otherwise?
translations.idiomatic: With the Yellow River ahead and the three prefectures behind, cautious planning at the crisis point left no other choice.

sentences.zh: 二帳、十二宮一府、五京，有兵一百六十四萬二千八百。

translations.literal: The two camps, twelve palaces, one office, and five capitals had troops totaling one million six hundred forty-two thousand eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Two imperial camps, twelve palaces, one office, and five capitals together fielded 1,642,800 troops.

sentences.zh: 宮丁、大首領、諸部族，中京、頭下等州，屬國之眾，皆不與焉。

translations.literal: Palace ding, great chieftains, all tribes, Zhongjing, subordinate prefectures, and subject peoples were not included.
translations.idiomatic: Palace levies, great chieftains, tribal hosts, Zhongjing, head-of-household domains, and subject troops lay outside this tally.

translations.literal: Not deploying them lightly was how the dynasty endured long.
translations.idiomatic: Restraint in committing them was how the dynasty lasted.

sentences.zh: 又得高麗《大遼事跡》，載東境戌兵，以備高麗、女直等國，見其守國規模，布置簡要，舉一可知三邊矣。

translations.literal: Goryeo's Great Liao Affairs also records eastern-border garrison troops against Goryeo, Jurchen, and other states—showing how the frontier was held in brief, telling arrangement; one example reveals all three borders.
translations.idiomatic: From Goryeo's record of Great Liao Affairs we also learn eastern garrisons facing Goryeo and Jurchen—a concise frontier layout from which all three borders can be inferred.

sentences.zh: 東京至鴨淥西北峰為界：黃龍府正兵五千。

translations.literal: From Eastern Capital to the Yalu's northwest peaks as the border: Huanglong Prefecture regular troops five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital frontier to the Yalu's northwest ridge: 5,000 regulars at Huanglong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 東京沿女直界至鴨淥江：軍堡凡七十，各守軍二十人，計正兵一千四百。

translations.literal: Along the Jurchen border from Eastern Capital to the Yalu River: seventy forts in all, each holding twenty men, totaling one thousand four hundred regulars.
translations.idiomatic: From Eastern Capital along the Jurchen line to the Yalu stood seventy forts with twenty men each—1,400 regulars in all.

sentences.zh: 來遠城宣義軍營八：太子營正兵三百。

translations.literal: Laiyuan City, Xuanyi Army, eight camps: Crown Prince Camp regular troops three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At Laiyuan's Xuanyi Army eight camps, the Crown Prince Camp held 300 regulars.
Great Camp: 600 militia levies of regulars.

translations.literal: Pu Prefecture Camp regular troops, 200 ding.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Prefecture Camp: 200 militia levies of regulars.
New Camp: 500 militia levies of regulars.
Jiata Camp: 500 militia levies of regulars.
Wanghai City garrisoned 300 militia levies of regulars.
Liubai Camp: 400 militia levies of regulars.
Woye Camp: 1,000 militia levies of regulars.
Shenhu City garrisoned 10,000 militia levies of regulars.
The post was founded in Dakang year 10.

sentences.zh: 右一府、一州、二城、七十堡、八營，計正兵二萬二千。

translations.literal: Right: one prefecture, one zhou, two cities, seventy forts, eight camps—regular troops totaling twenty-two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Totals: one prefecture, one zhou, two cities, seventy forts, eight camps—22,000 regular troops.
